summary: P031 r9 is a materially corrected proposal: an operator-driven narrowing from GraphQL+MCP thin-client control cutover (r7) to a GraphQL-only read/inspection cutover. The macOS UI becomes a pure renderer of server projections with no MCP, no GraphQL mutations, and no local workflow writes. All four reviewers approve directionally but the architect identifies one blocking issue: the P043 reference contract still describes P031 as owning command-completion and MCP-control UI behavior, creating a dependency-contract conflict with the r9 no-UI-write rule. Product owner (8/10) approves with conditions around documenting the operator write-path workflow and adding user-outcome metrics. UX designer (8.5/10) approves but flags approval task flow fragmentation. UI designer (8/10) approves with comments on Syncing placement in detail views and approval visual coherence. Architect (8/10) approves with conditions but blocks on P043 contract reconciliation plus three medium non-blocking issues around schema field mapping, UI file boundary, and approval disabled-state contract.

required_changes.title: P043 reference contract still conflicts with the GraphQL-only P031 correction
required_changes.required_change: Before Phase 1, amend P043 reference and any composed P031 gate language so command-completion refresh, command receipt display, and MCP command-control rules are explicitly outside P031-owned UI. Keep MCP command behavior documented for non-UI agents/CLI/diagnostics.

required_changes.title: Read-only disabled/report/approval metadata is not mapped to concrete GraphQL schema fields
required_changes.required_change: Add a concrete schema matrix for each new read-only field: GraphQL type/query, enum cases, nullability, principal redaction, Swift presenter owner, and tests.

required_changes.title: Static-guard boundary depends on an undefined P031-owned UI file set
required_changes.required_change: Define the Phase 0 UI ownership inventory: exact Swift files/types in scope, legacy-only files, generated GraphQL operation locations, forbidden import/call patterns, and explicit exclusions.

required_changes.title: Approval decisions remain a boundary exception without an implementation-safe disabled-state contract
required_changes.required_change: Make approval decision behavior binary: either hidden/read-only diagnostics only, or enabled through a named separately approved transport with its own proposal and tests. No Swift inference of write availability.

required_changes.title: Source-governance drift between run-local contract and checked-in proposal
required_changes.required_change: Promote the full r9 contract or add a checked-in implementation addendum that marks the run-local artifact as governing and copies Phase 0 obligations.

required_changes.title: No documented operator workflow for write operations during the write-removed period
required_changes.required_change: Before dogfood start, publish an operator guide mapping each removed P031 UI write control to its current alternative surface or explicitly marking it temporarily unavailable with a follow-up reference.

required_changes.title: Fragmented task flow for approval decisions
required_changes.required_change: Replace disabled primary button with a distinct UI element (e.g., inline banner or terminal-styled text box) that says 'Execute via CLI' with copyable ID, or hide the control entirely.

required_changes.title: Ambiguous placement of Syncing pattern in detail views
required_changes.required_change: Explicitly define Syncing pattern placement for RunDetailView and ArtifactsView (e.g., top trailing edge of navigation bar or fixed header slot) to ensure no layout shift in detail screens.

required_changes.title: Vague Report payload availability indicators
required_changes.required_change: Specify the exact icon family or text truncation rules for report payload availability to prevent inconsistent density in the Reports list.

recurring_themes.theme: Approval control liminal state and disabled UX
recurring_themes.description: All four reviewers converge on the approval decision surface as the riskiest UX/architecture seam. The architect (ARCH-R9-04) wants a binary disabled-state contract. The UX designer (UX-R9-01) flags 'tease and block' UX. The UI designer (UI-02) flags visual coherence of permanently disabled primary buttons. The product owner (PO-R9-04) wants explicit dogfood validation of operator comprehension. This is the single highest-convergence theme.

The architect (ARCH-R9-01, blocking) identifies that P043 still describes P031 as owning MCP command-control UI behavior. This is a dependency-contract conflict, not stale wording, and must be resolved before Phase 1.

The product owner (PO-R9-01) and UX designer (UX-R9-02) both flag that removing all write controls without documenting the alternative operator workflow creates an untestable dogfood gap. The PO wants an operator guide before dogfood; the UX wants in-UI guidance to the actual destination.

recurring_themes.theme: Schema field concreteness for new read-only metadata
recurring_themes.description: The architect (ARCH-R9-02) wants concrete GraphQL types and redaction rules for new disabled/report/approval metadata fields. The UI designer (UI-03) wants specific icon family for report payload availability. Both converge on the need for implementation-ready schema specificity.

recurring_themes.theme: UI file/module boundary for static guards
recurring_themes.description: The architect (ARCH-R9-03) flags that static guards depend on an undefined set of P031-owned UI files. Without a path inventory, guards can miss bypasses or block legitimate legacy rollback code.
